source.method: Manual reading of every ledger state cell, cross-checked against cited tracked artifacts and the current DP-2/MT-8 packets; no status inferred from keyword position alone.

coverage.counts_note: A logical-ID total is used here: HC-4 and HC-5 are split. The table has 74 physical rows because they are folded in one row. A row can be partial and still require work; open_gated includes named prerequisites.

DP-2.coverage: 12 canonical + 16 heldout; 3 measured repetitions per arm; D128; p512 control, p1024 control, p4096 admission
DP-2.decision: No production promotion: p4096 prefill is +0.189% in this complete-engine run despite the native owner saving; candidate remains opt-in/default-off.

MT-8.coverage: all rejection depths plus full accept
MT-8.decision: No duplicate target replay or dirty-destination restore exists in the screened route; no production change.

remaining_high_value_or_blocked.gate: Implement and run the F16 expert owner; complete production numerical/task gate; preserve strict fallback.
Re-run/close the chunk-4096 qualification against the corrected X-6 gate; do not promote from the stale/vacuous gate.
Separate complete-operation/native ownership screen for any further promotion; current 4096 handoff is bounded and not a universal claim.
Compose the existing rowbatch kernel into a complete verifier body and measure it; current kernel-pair screen is not end-to-end.
Establish same-protocol comparator/quality basis before setting a target.
Finish current qualification, scope-policy, stability and long-task engagement certificates; partial local fixes are not full qualification.

claims_not_supported: No whole-model promotion follows from the DP-2 native operation saving or the rows-4096 engine A/B.
MT-8's zero restored bytes/allocations are accounting results, not native GPU allocation measurements.
The census does not close X-1/X-3/X-5/X-6/X-7 or any partial row; it records the missing gate explicitly.
The 75 logical-ID count is not comparable to earlier 72/74 counts without applying the HC-4/HC-5 split.
